ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached power-circle diagram shows P and Q axes, with circular arc loci drawn around the operating construction. A marked operating point lies on the right side of the circle, with a slanted line through or near that point indicating the power-factor direction/angle. The diagram also includes a voltage-related circular construction labeled near U, and a lower angle construction indicating the power angle. Reasoning: If the power factor angle is kept unchanged, the operating/load point must stay on the same power-factor direction rather than moving to another power-factor line. When the sending-end voltage increases, the corresponding power-circle construction associated with the sending voltage expands or shifts. The new operating intersection on the unchanged power-factor direction is located so that the lower angle construction for the power angle becomes larger. Therefore, under unchanged power factor angle, increasing the sending-end voltage makes the power angle increase.
